result:
All tests pass (51/51), and this is the only `*AgentTest.java` file in the project, so that's the full suite.

I created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtilsAgentTest.java`, a self-contained JUnit 5 test class covering `DateUtils`: the `add*`/`set*` mutators (including range-validation and null-argument errors), `ceiling`/`round`/`truncate` for `Calendar`/`Date`/`Object` overloads (including `SEMI_MONTH`/`AM_PM` special cases, unsupported-field and huge-year `ArithmeticException` cases), fragment getters, `isSameDay`/`isSameInstant`/`isSameLocalTime`, the day-range `iterator` (including exhaustion, invalid range style, and unsupported `remove()`), lenient vs. strict `parseDate`/`parseDateStrictly`, `toCalendar`/`toLocalDateTime`/`toOffsetDateTime`/`toZonedDateTime`, `truncatedCompareTo`/`truncatedEquals`, and the public constants/constructor.

One note: a couple of edge-case behaviors I initially assumed from the javadoc (e.g. `getFragmentInMinutes` with a `MONTH` fragment, and the zone ID returned by `toZonedDateTime` for UTC) didn't match the actual runtime behavior, so I verified them empirically against the compiled class before asserting on them.
